memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps. He must burn incense again when he lights the lamps at twilight so incense will burn regularly before the Lord for the generations to come." - Exodus 30:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Incense burned twice daily, morning and evening, tied to the tending of the lamps. As Aaron trimmed the wicks, he also set the incense burning. Care for the light and the rising of prayer happened together, at the start and close of each day.

Notice the word "regularly." God did not want occasional bursts of incense followed by long gaps of cold ashes. He wanted a steady, unbroken fragrance rising before Him across generations. Consistency mattered more than intensity.

Most of us would rather have dramatic spiritual moments than daily faithfulness, but God builds through the ordinary and repeated. Daniel prayed three times a day, and Scripture notes that this was simply what he had always done (Dan 6:10). The habit was already there when the crisis came. If prayer is only what you reach for in emergencies, it will feel unfamiliar precisely when you most need it. Light the incense today, and again tomorrow. Regular is better than remarkable.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Is my prayer life regular, or mostly reserved for emergencies?
What small, sustainable rhythm could I begin this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You value steady faithfulness above occasional intensity. Build in me a regular rhythm of prayer, so that turning to You becomes natural rather than exceptional. Amen.
